Its use for regression at the regular design in the trigonometric system follows the analyses of R. Shibata (Biometrika 68 (1981), 45–54) and J. Rice (Ann. Statist. 12 (1984), 1215–1230).

title: Discrete Orthonormality of the Trigonometric Basis at the Regular Design
informal:
Let $\{\varphi_j\}_{j \ge 1}$ be the trigonometric basis of $L^2[0,1]$. Then the first $n-1$ basis functions are exactly orthonormal also in the discrete inner product generated by the regular design $x_s = s/n$: for all indices $1 \le j \le n-1$ and $1 \le k \le n-1$, $$\frac{1}{n} \sum_{s=1}^{n} \varphi_j(s/n)\, \varphi_k(s/n) \;=\; \delta_{jk},$$ where $\delta_{jk}$ is the Kronecker delta.

Equivalently, the empirical Gram matrix of $\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_{n-1}$ at the regular design is the identity — the discrete counterpart of the orthonormality relation $\int_0^1 \varphi_j \varphi_k = \delta_{jk}$. This is the reason the coefficient estimates $\hat\theta_j$ of the projection estimator behave exactly like Fourier coefficients: the stochastic part of their risk is exactly $\sigma_\xi^2/n$, with no cross-frequency contamination below index $n$.
summary: The first n−1 trigonometric basis functions are exactly orthonormal in the discrete inner product n⁻¹ Σₛ φⱼ(s/n)φₖ(s/n) at the regular design.
leanSignature:
theorem trigBasis_discrete_orthonormal {n j k : ℕ}
    (hj : 1 ≤ j) (hj' : j ≤ n - 1) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hk' : k ≤ n - 1) :
    (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i : Fin n, trigBasis j (regularDesign n i) * trigBasis k (regularDesign n i)
      = if j = k then 1 else 0
formalizationNotes: The statement is the book's identity with the Kronecker delta rendered as an if-then-else and the design sum over `i : Fin n` (design points $(i+1)/n = 1/n, \dots, 1$). The proof reduces each product $\varphi_j\varphi_k$ by product-to-sum identities to discrete cosine/sine sums at the integer frequencies $j/2 \pm k/2$, which — by exact roots-of-unity summation — vanish unless the frequency is a multiple of $n$; the range $1 \le j, k \le n-1$ keeps these frequencies inside $(-n, n)$, so only the zero frequency survives, precisely at equal same-parity indices, where the normalization $(\sqrt2)^2 \cdot \tfrac12 = 1$ gives the diagonal. The book proves one representative parity case and leaves the rest 'along similar lines'; the Lean proof covers all nine parity cases. The continuous companion `trigBasis_orthonormal` establishes the $L^2[0,1]$ orthonormality $\int_0^1 \varphi_j\varphi_k = \delta_{jk}$ for all $j, k \ge 1$.

hypotheses.label: index range for j
hypotheses.note: 1 ≤ j ≤ n − 1: the frequency of φⱼ stays below the design size; beyond n − 1 exact orthonormality fails (aliasing).

hypotheses.label: index range for k
hypotheses.note: 1 ≤ k ≤ n − 1, the same range for the second index.

reference.formal: A. B. Tsybakov, *Introduction to Nonparametric Estimation*, Springer, New York, 2009.
reference.pointer: §1.7.2 (Integrated squared risk of projection estimators), Lemma 1.7
reference.biblio: The identity is classical discrete Fourier analysis — exact orthogonality of the sampled trigonometric system, equivalently of the $n$-th roots of unity. Its role in regular-design series regression appears in J. Rice (Ann. Statist. 12 (1984), 1215–1230); the behaviour of the discrete products beyond the first $n-1$ frequencies — the aliasing this lemma rules out — is studied by B. T. Polyak and A. B. Tsybakov (Theory Probab. Appl. 35 (1990), 293–306).

title: Mean and Quadratic Risk of the Coefficient Estimates
informal:
Consider the regression model $Y_i = f(i/n) + \xi_i$, $i = 1, \dots, n$, at the regular design, where the target has the trigonometric expansion $f = \sum_{j \ge 1} \theta_j \varphi_j$ with absolutely summable coefficients $\sum_j |\theta_j| < \infty$, and the errors $\xi_1, \dots, \xi_n$ are independent with $\mathbb{E}[\xi_i] = 0$ and common second moment $\mathbb{E}[\xi_i^2] = \sigma_\xi^2 < \infty$. Then the coefficient estimates $\hat\theta_j = n^{-1} \sum_{i} Y_i \varphi_j(i/n)$ satisfy $\mathbb{E}[\hat\theta_j] = \theta_j + \alpha_j$ for every $j$, and, for every index $1 \le j \le n-1$, the exact quadratic-risk identity $$\mathbb{E}\big[(\hat\theta_j - \theta_j)^2\big] \;=\; \frac{\sigma_\xi^2}{n} + \alpha_j^2, \qquad \alpha_j = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} f(i/n)\, \varphi_j(i/n) \;-\; \theta_j.$$

Here $\alpha_j$ is the residual of approximating the Fourier coefficient $\theta_j = \int_0^1 f \varphi_j$ by its Riemann sum over the design — the aliasing bias of the discretization. The entire stochastic contribution to the risk is exactly $\sigma_\xi^2/n$, a consequence of the discrete orthonormality of the trigonometric basis at the regular design (Lemma 1.7).
summary: Coefficient estimates satisfy E θ̂ⱼ = θⱼ + αⱼ and, for 1 ≤ j ≤ n−1, E(θ̂ⱼ − θⱼ)² = σ_ξ²/n + αⱼ² exactly, where αⱼ is the Riemann-sum (aliasing) residual.

theorem coeffEstimator_sq_error {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure P] {n : ℕ} {ξ : Fin n → Ω → ℝ} {θ : ℕ → ℝ} {σξ2 : ℝ} {j : ℕ}
    (hj : 1 ≤ j) (hj' : j ≤ n - 1)
    (hσ : 0 ≤ σξ2)
    (hθ1 : Summable fun j => |θ j|)
    (hξm : ∀ i, Measurable (ξ i))
    (hξi : iIndepFun ξ P)
    (hξ0 : ∀ i, ∫ ω, ξ i ω ∂P = 0)
    (hξ2 : ∀ i, ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal ((ξ i ω) ^ 2) ∂P = ENNReal.ofReal σξ2) :
    ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal
        ((coeffEstimator (fun i => seriesFun θ (regularDesign n i) + ξ i ω) j - θ j) ^ 2) ∂P
      = ENNReal.ofReal (σξ2 / n + (riemannResidual θ n j) ^ 2)

title: Exact MISE Decomposition of the Projection Estimator
informal:
In the regression model $Y_i = f(i/n) + \xi_i$ at the regular design, with target $f = \sum_{j \ge 1} \theta_j \varphi_j$, $\sum_j |\theta_j| < \infty$, and independent errors of mean zero and common second moment $\sigma_\xi^2$, the mean integrated squared error of the projection estimator $\hat f_{nN} = \sum_{j=1}^{N} \hat\theta_j \varphi_j$ of any order $1 \le N \le n-1$ decomposes exactly: $$\mathbb{E}\,\big\|\hat f_{nN} - f\big\|_2^2 \;=\; \frac{\sigma_\xi^2 N}{n} \;+\; \sum_{j=1}^{N} \alpha_j^2 \;+\; \rho_N, \qquad \rho_N = \sum_{j=N+1}^{\infty} \theta_j^2,$$ where $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the $L^2$ norm on $[0,1]$ and $\alpha_j = n^{-1}\sum_i f(i/n)\varphi_j(i/n) - \theta_j$ is the Riemann-sum residual of Proposition 1.16.

The three terms are the stochastic (variance) term $\sigma_\xi^2 N/n$, the aliasing term $\sum_{j \le N} \alpha_j^2$, and the approximation term $\rho_N$ — the energy of the discarded coefficient tail. This exact identity is the starting point of the risk analysis of series estimators over Sobolev classes.
summary: Exact MISE identity for the projection estimator: E‖f̂_nN − f‖₂² = σ_ξ²N/n + Σ_{j≤N} αⱼ² + ρ_N, with tail energy ρ_N = Σ_{j>N} θⱼ².

    (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hN' : N ≤ n - 1)
    (hσ : 0 ≤ σξ2)
    (hθ1 : Summable fun j => |θ j|)
    (hξm : ∀ i, Measurable (ξ i))
    (hξi : iIndepFun ξ P)
    (hξ0 : ∀ i, ∫ ω, ξ i ω ∂P = 0)
    (hξ2 : ∀ i, ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal ((ξ i ω) ^ 2) ∂P = ENNReal.ofReal σξ2) :
    ∫⁻ ω, (∫⁻ x in Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ENNReal.ofReal
        ((projEstimator (fun i => seriesFun θ (regularDesign n i) + ξ i ω) N x
          - seriesFun θ x) ^ 2)) ∂P
      = ENNReal.ofReal (σξ2 * N / n
          + (∑ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (riemannResidual θ n j) ^ 2) + tailEnergy θ N)
formalizationNotes: The conclusion is an exact identity, not a bound. The book leaves the admissible range of $N$ implicit (its proof invokes Proposition 1.16(ii) for every $j \le N$); the formal statement makes $1 \le N \le n-1$ explicit. The expectation is formalized as an iterated lower Lebesgue integral in the extended reals — the mean over the sample of $\int_{[0,1]} (\hat f_{nN} - f)^2$ — so no integrability assumptions are laundered, and the right-hand side is the finite real value of the decomposition. Because the target is defined as `seriesFun θ`, the tail's squared $L^2$ norm is proved equal to `tailEnergy θ N` $= \sum_{j>N}\theta_j^2$ via uniform convergence of the tail series and the $L^2$ orthonormality `trigBasis_orthonormal` — no completeness of the trigonometric system (Parseval) is invoked anywhere.

title: MISE Rate of the Projection Estimator over Sobolev Ellipsoids
informal:
Let $\beta \ge 1$ and $L > 0$, and consider the Sobolev class of targets $f = \sum_{j \ge 1} \theta_j \varphi_j$ whose coefficient sequence lies in the Sobolev ellipsoid $\Theta(\beta, Q) = \big\{\theta : \sum_{j \ge 1} a_j^2 \theta_j^2 \le Q\big\}$ of radius $Q = L^2/\pi^{2\beta}$, with the standard weights $a_j = j^{\beta}$ for even $j$ and $a_j = (j-1)^{\beta}$ for odd $j$. Observations follow the regression model $Y_i = f(i/n) + \xi_i$ at the regular design $i/n$, with independent errors of mean zero and common second moment $\sigma_\xi^2$. For a tuning constant $\alpha > 0$, choose the order $N = \big\lceil \alpha\, n^{1/(2\beta+1)} \big\rceil$.

Then there is a constant $C = C(\beta, L, \alpha, \sigma_\xi^2) > 0$ such that for every sample size with $n \ge 3$ and $N \le n-1$ (both hold for all $n$ large enough), the projection estimator $\hat f_{nN} = \sum_{j=1}^{N} \hat\theta_j \varphi_j$ satisfies $$\mathbb{E}\,\big\|\hat f_{nN} - f\big\|_2^2 \;\le\; C\, n^{-\frac{2\beta}{2\beta+1}}$$ uniformly over the class and over every error distribution satisfying these conditions. The projection estimator thus attains the rate $n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}$ in the $L^2[0,1]$ norm on the Sobolev class — the same rate as for pointwise estimation over Hölder classes.
summary: With N ≈ αn^(1/(2β+1)), the projection estimator attains MISE ≤ C n^(−2β/(2β+1)) uniformly over the Sobolev ellipsoid Θ(β, L²/π^(2β)), for smoothness β ≥ 1.

theorem proj_sobolev_rate {β L α σξ2 : ℝ}
    (hβ : 1 ≤ β) (hL : 0 < L) (hα : 0 < α) (hσ : 0 ≤ σξ2) :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
      ∀ {n N : ℕ},
        3 ≤ n → N = ⌈α * (n : ℝ) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (2 * β + 1))⌉₊ → N ≤ n - 1 →
      ∀ {θ : ℕ → ℝ},
        MemEllipsoid β (ellipsoidRadius β L) θ →
      ∀ {Ω : Type} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P]
        (ξ : Fin n → Ω → ℝ),
        (∀ i, Measurable (ξ i)) → iIndepFun ξ P →
        (∀ i, ∫ ω, ξ i ω ∂P = 0) →
        (∀ i, ∫⁻ ω, ENNReal.ofReal ((ξ i ω) ^ 2) ∂P = ENNReal.ofReal σξ2) →
        ∫⁻ ω, (∫⁻ x in Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ENNReal.ofReal
            ((projEstimator (fun i => seriesFun θ (regularDesign n i) + ξ i ω) N x
              - seriesFun θ x) ^ 2)) ∂P
          ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * (n : ℝ) ^ (-(2 * β / (2 * β + 1))))
formalizationNotes: Finite-$n$ form of the book's asymptotic statement: the bound holds for every $n \ge 3$ with $N \le n-1$, uniformly in $\theta$, in the probability space, and in the error distribution, which implies the book's limsup-of-sup form; $C$ is a sanctioned existential (the book's constant is unspecified) and depends on $\beta, L, \alpha$ and also on $\sigma_\xi^2$, which the book fixes implicitly in Assumption (A). The order uses the ceiling $N = \lceil \alpha n^{1/(2\beta+1)} \rceil$ rather than the book's integer part, guaranteeing $N \ge 1$. The aliasing term is controlled by the formalized Lemma 1.8, `riemannResidual_abs_le`: $|\alpha_j| \le C_{\beta,Q}\, n^{1/2-\beta}$ for $1 \le j \le n-1$ with the explicit constant `residualConst` $C_{\beta,Q} = 2\sqrt{Q}\,\sqrt{2\beta/(2\beta-1)}\, 3^{\beta-1/2}$ (the factor $3^{\beta-1/2}$ absorbs a tail-shift estimate valid for $n \ge 3$ — the origin of the side condition, versus the book's $n \ge 2$). Assumption (A)(iii), $\sum_j |\theta_j| < \infty$, is never assumed: on the ellipsoid with $\beta \ge 1 > 1/2$ it is derived via `MemEllipsoid.summable_abs`. Risks are lower Lebesgue integrals in the extended reals so no integrability is laundered, and `MemEllipsoid` carries convergence of the weighted series as a constitutive field, ruling out vacuous junk-value membership.
